extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to systematically evaluate multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five cognitive dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6,092 QA pairs across diverse embodiments, objects, viewpoints, and task settings.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data combine high-quality open-source large-scale real-world robotic datasets and curated in-house collection. It extracts frame sequences from robotic videos across single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile manipulation embodiments, static/functional object attributes, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source real-world robotic datasets (such as RH20T, Open X-Embodiment, RDT-1B, RoboMIND, AgiBot World Colosseo, etc.) and in-house collected robotic video data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: General and task-specific filters were applied during construction to address image quality, task validity, and sub-benchmark constraints (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks). Items that all models solved correctly were removed, and items all models failed to solve underwent manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations followed dimension-specific workflows using MLLMs (such as Gemini for video segmentation, task summaries, step-wise instructions, and timestamps; LLMs for rewriting explicit instructions to implicit requests) and human expert annotations (refining steps, relative positions, keypoint changes, spatial relations, causal reasoning, bounding boxes, DAG dependency construction, and affordance points/trajectories). A two-stage quality control included data filtering and post-construction inspection by 20 professionally trained annotators using a majority-vote strategy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Adopted a majority-vote strategy and manual review: items solved correctly by all models were removed to prevent saturation, while items failed by all models underwent manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current MLLMs exhibit severe degradation on implicit instructions, struggle with robotic-view recognition, causal/spatiotemporal reasoning, dual-arm coordination, mobile manipulation, rare-object reasoning, fine-grained affordance prediction, and execution-level failure diagnosis. Planning-level failure data had to be synthesized due to a lack of real-world planning failure data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) acting as the high-level cognitive brain (System 2) in robotic manipulation tasks across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.
